The petitioner is an accused in connection with Itamati P.S. Case No.87 of 2025 corresponding to G.R. Case No.340 of 2025 registered for the alleged commission of the offences punishable under Sections 376/294/ 506/451/323/354/34 of the IPC, pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M.,
Nayagarh.
The petitioner had approached the learned Sessions Judge, Nayagarh in BLAPL No.122 of 2025 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 07.04.2025 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.
The prosecution case is that, on 26.03.2025, the complainant reported at the P.S. that she knows the present petitioner since the year 2022.
The petitioner was regularly visiting her house.
On 14.02.2023, the petitioner came to her house when her family members were not in the house and forcibly raped her without her consent.
She informed the matter to her family members.
The petitioner assured to marry her.
Subsequently, the petitioner kept physical relationship with her regularly.
On 20.03.2025, she came to know that the petitioner is arranging his marriage with another girl.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4
. During the investigation, the statement of the victim, who is 24 years of age, was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
She in her statement has stated that she was in relationship with the petitioner.
Since last two years, the petitioner had promised to marry her and kept physical relationship with her.
But subsequently he wriggled out of his promise.
5. Mr. Saswat Kumar Sethi, learned counsel has entered appearance on behalf of the victim.

The victim has filed an affidavit dated 08.05.2025 before this Court, inter alia, stating as under:
"2. That it is respectfully submitted here that I have lodged the present case against the petitioner due to some misunderstanding between us and now with the intervention of family members and further taking into consideration about my future marriage for which myself is not interested to proceed further in this case.

3. That it is respectfully submitted here that in the facts and circumstances of the present case this deponent do not want to proceed further in the aforesaid case against the present petitioner and I have no objection, if your Lordship allows the Bail Application of the present petitioner."

6. Regard being had to the nature of allegation against the petitioner and the period of custody since 28.03.2025 and the fact that the victim has filed an affidavit before this Court that due to the misunderstanding, she had lodged the F.I.R. against the petitioner and in the statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. as well, she has stated that she was in relationship with the petitioner, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

In the event, the petitioner is found to be wanted for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
